weather.tip: With an 86% chance of rain and Deepavali outflow on the same roads, book your cab or bus before leaving; and if you're heading for the airport, the Ballari Road curbs mean leaving earlier than usual.

edge.title: Meter politics at the junction
edge.setup: Diwali evening, rain on the way, and everyone is heading out at once. The auto refuses the meter and quotes a flat fare, double. There is no other auto in sight, you're late, and he knows all three. This is not fraud — it's a negotiation where he currently holds every card.
edge.tell: If you're arguing about the price, you've already accepted that he's the only option.
move: Change where you stand. Walk 100m to the main road; scarcity was the only leverage he had.
Open an app and let him watch. The visible alternative resets the price more reliably than argument.
If you need the formal route: the refusal, auto number and location go to the Bengaluru Traffic Police app or 080-22868550. Mentioning you're noting the number often ends the matter.
Never start with anger. Start with the alternative — anger is a worse tool than a visible option.
edge.why: Price is set by alternatives, not by fairness. Every effective move here manufactures an alternative — distance, an app, a complaint channel — rather than appealing to rules. This is the whole of negotiation in miniature.
edge.variants: Same shape: surge pricing you can wait out, 'last room available' at a hotel desk, the mechanic who found three more problems.

lens.name: Compounding
lens.one_line: Small consistent changes beat big sporadic ones, because the result is multiplicative, not additive.
lens.detail: Intuition is linear; compounding isn't, which is why almost everyone underestimates it. ₹5,000 a month at 12% is about ₹11 lakh in 10 years and roughly ₹50 lakh in 20 — most of that gain arriving in the final stretch. The same shape governs skills, reputation and debt. Credit-card interest at 3.5% a month is this force running against you at roughly 50% a year.
elsewhere: Minimum card payments keeping a balance alive for years.
Reputation: slow to build, then suddenly everything arrives at once.
lens.test: Is this a one-time event, or something that multiplies? Multiplying things deserve disproportionate attention.
lens.today: The Sensex is reported up 10.6% in seven pre-Diwali sessions, its best run in 35 years (Times of India). A run like that feels like a trend, but it is a sporadic jump, not the steady multiplication the detail above describes. What compounds for you is the boring part: a fixed monthly amount invested, and the festival bonus kept out of the first-week spend.

moved.what: Bengaluru Traffic Police has identified 7 alternative routes and restricted KSRTC bus movement on Ballari Road for the BDA's ₹725 crore elevated corridor, with restrictions expected for 18 months (Deccan Herald, NDTV).
moved.so_what: If your trip touches Hebbal, Mekhri Circle or the airport road, pick your alternative route in advance and add buffer time. The Times of India asks whether those routes become new hotspots.

moved.what: Moneycontrol reports that construction work by BDA, BIAL and NHAI could delay the airport commute.
moved.so_what: For any flight in the coming weeks, plan your road time against the worst case, not the usual one.

moved.what: Urban Acres reports Bengaluru's special Diwali buses are spread across 11 hubs.
moved.so_what: If you're travelling out, check which hub your bus leaves from before you set off, rather than assuming the usual stand.

moved.what: The Times of India reports that Karnataka lab tests show 'excess' ethanol in petrol, with the headline asking whether it is E20 or E31.
moved.so_what: If your mileage has dropped, note the pump and fill date; a pattern at one pump is worth a complaint.

moved.what: A consumer commission ordered an airline to refund ₹11,587 and pay ₹50,000 compensation plus ₹10,000 costs after it marked a passenger a 'no-show' without CCTV or other evidence of late arrival (Times of India).
moved.so_what: If an airline marks you a no-show, keep your timestamps and check-in photos; the burden of evidence falls on whoever has the footage.

moved.what: The Sensex rose 10.6% over seven pre-Diwali sessions, its best run in 35 years (Times of India).
moved.so_what: Don't treat a record week as a forecast; keep your monthly investment amount fixed rather than raising it after a rally.

carry_over.prompt: A loose-sweets counter has no date on the tray and the shopkeeper says it was 'made fresh this morning' — what is your test?
carry_over.answer: If nobody can show you a date on the tray or a food licence number on the wall, 'fresh this morning' is just a sentence.
